sections.skill: Match tasks to what AI tools do well and poorly

questions.domain: Foundation 12: AI as a practical helper
questions.prompt: Which task suits an AI tool well?

choices.text: Drafting a first version of a product description
Confirming this year's exact tax rules with certainty
Knowing which local customers will definitely buy
Deciding the final legal structure for the business alone

questions.correct_answer: Drafting a first version of a product description
questions.intro: AI tools (programs that generate text, images or summaries from a request) can save time on DRAFTING and ORGANIZING work: a first draft of a product description, a summary of long notes, ideas for a social post, a list of questions to ask a supplier, or reformatting a price list. They are weaker at work that needs verified facts, legal or tax certainty, or knowledge of your specific customers. A good rule: let the tool draft, and let a person who knows the business check and decide.

questions.intro: Imagine hiring a very fast assistant on their first day. They can type a draft letter in minutes and tidy a messy list, but they do not know your customers, your prices, or the law, and they sometimes guess confidently. You would let them draft, then read it before anything is sent. An AI tool is like that assistant: helpful for drafts, not a replacement for your judgment.
